facts.title: Areni-1
facts.text: In southern Armenia, this cave houses the oldest known winery on Earth.

facts.title: A clay press
facts.text: Boris Gasparyan and his team uncover a rudimentary clay press: the first traces of winemaking.

facts.title: 6,100 years
facts.text: The oldest winemaking facility ever found is formally announced, dating to the 4th millennium BCE.

facts.title: An inclined surface
facts.text: Grapes were crushed on it, and the juice drained into a large collection vat dug into the ground.

facts.title: A ritual wine
facts.text: Wine consumption held ritual significance during ceremonial gatherings.

facts.title: A 5,500-year-old shoe
facts.text: Cut from cowhide, size 37, it predates the one found on the Alpine mummy Ötzi.

facts.title: A fundamental milestone
facts.text: Through the splendor of its winemaking installations, Areni-1 stands out in the history and heritage of Armenia.

ytTitle: Areni-1, the oldest known winery on Earth, in Armenia
ytLead: In the Areni-1 cave, in the heart of Vayots Dzor, excavations carried out since 2007 have unearthed a 6,100-year-old winemaking facility, the oldest ever found.
